text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Democratic Left Party (DSP) leader Bulent Ecevit rules out a unification of the DSP with another leftist party.
- The deputy head of Turkey's armed forces Cevik Bir says during a speech in Washington that Iran should be treated as a terrorist state.
- Iran's ambassador and consul-general finally leave Turkey after drawing secularist criticism for comments advocating the establishment of sharia, or Islamic law, in Turkey.
- A former state minister and opposition MP says the government's aim of achieving a balanced budget is illusory.
- State Minister Abdullah Gul disappoints U.S. officials during a visit to the United States despite hopes for his trip and his extremely careful and moderate stance.
- An official at the U.S. State Department says the United States may be obliged to impose sanctions if an oil pipeline is built between Iran and Turkey.
- The cost of delays in the construction of the Istanbul metro amounts to $100,000 a day.
- Official pressure is increasing to curb nightly protests which began at the start of February against a security scandal in Turkey.
- State Ziraat Bankasi has requested the return of a 750 million mark credit to Turkey's export-import Eximbank.
- The nightly protests against a security scandal are increasingly deviating from their aim.
